# EvSlider

> A slider lets users select a value or range by dragging a handle along a track, giving direct, continuous control over a bounded numeric input.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:slider` |
| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |
| Import | `import { EvSlider } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvSlider>` or `<ev-slider>` |
| Source | `src/atoms/slider/EvSlider.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<div class="ev-slider">` |

## Example

```vue
<EvSlider
  :model-value="40"
  show-value
/>
```

## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Slider**, frame `4510:85163` (Slider). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use for selecting a value or range within a known min–max where approximate, visual adjustment is natural — volume, brightness, price range, zoom.

### When not to use

- Don't use when an exact number matters — use a number input. Don't use for a small set of discrete options — use a segmented control or radio group (`evoq-ui:radio-group`).

### Do

- Show the current value near the handle, and use Range when both a lower and upper bound are needed. Provide a sensible default position.

### Don't

- Don't use the Destructive variant for routine adjustments — reserve it for values with damaging consequences. Don't make the track so short that precise control is hard.

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvSlider`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<div class="ev-slider">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:slider` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
